text_blocks.snippet: Early signs of type 2 diabetes develop slowly and often include increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue.
snippet_highlighted_words: increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue

list.snippet: Increased thirst and frequent urination: High blood sugar forces your kidneys to work overtime to flush out extra sugar, which pulls water from your tissues and makes you need the bathroom more often.
Constant fatigue: Your cells cannot properly absorb glucose (sugar) from your blood to use for energy, leaving you feeling drained even after resting.
Blurred vision: Extra sugar in your blood can pull fluid from the lenses in your eyes, making it hard to focus.
Slow-healing cuts and sores: High blood sugar impairs blood circulation and immune response, making minor wounds take much longer to heal.
Frequent infections: Bacteria and yeast thrive on excess sugar, leading to more frequent urinary tract or skin infections.
Darkened skin patches: Velvety, dark skin patches—known as acanthosis nigricans—often appear on the neck or armpits as a sign of insulin resistance.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about official warning signs from the American Diabetes Association or read the comprehensive overview on Mayo Clinic.

perspectives.title: 🚨 5 warning signs your body may be developing insulin resistance or prediabetes. Don’t ignore them. Diabetes doesn’t always appear overnight. Your body often gives subtle warning signs months or even years before blood sugar levels become severely abnormal. ⚠️ Watch out for these common symptoms: ✔️ Constant fatigue despite adequate sleep ✔️ Tingling or numbness in your hands and feet ✔️ Excessive hunger and excessive thirst ✔️ Frequent urination, especially at night ✔️ Dark, velvety patches around the neck, underarms, knees, or knuckles (Acanthosis Nigricans) These symptoms can be associated with insulin resistance a condition that often develops before type 2 diabetes. While these signs don’t confirm diabetes on their own, they are important reasons to get evaluated. Early diagnosis and lifestyle changes can significantly reduce the risk of developing type 2 diabetes. 💬 Have you noticed any of these symptoms?
